punchline: The internet made gathering a tribe cheap, so the hard part left is being willing to lead it.
thirty_sec: Seth Godin calls a group connected to each other, to a leader and to an idea a tribe. The internet removed the problem of distance, so anyone can find people who share their outlook. What holds most people back is being visible, because leading invites criticism. His view is that leading needs a point of view and a steady voice, with no title attached.
question: Is there a group you belong to that you found online, and how did you first end up in it?
